headline: Earnings plunge on a tax-rate spike and rising pay costs
summary_short: Lazard's Q2 2026 diluted EPS fell to $0.03 from $0.52 a year ago as net income attributable to Lazard dropped 91% y/y to $4.8M, even as net revenue rose 1% y/y to $807.7M.
summary_long: Net revenue rose 1% y/y to $807.7M: Asset Management net revenue jumped 20% on higher average AUM and management fees (+23%), while Financial Advisory net revenue fell 9% on fewer completed M&A fees. Compensation expense rose 8% to $562.4M, lifting the adjusted comp ratio to 69.9% from 65.5%; non-compensation expense rose 13% on Campbell Lutyens deal costs. Operating income fell 60% to $37.6M. The effective tax rate jumped to 63.5% from 34.1% on a first-quarter share-based-compensation tax catch-up and geographic mix, driving net income attributable to Lazard down 91% to $4.8M (diluted EPS $0.03). Subsequent to quarter-end, the board declared a $0.50/share dividend and added $200M of buyback authorization.

drivers.explanation: Net revenue grew 1% as 20% growth in Asset Management fees offset a 9% decline in Financial Advisory fees, but comp expense grew faster than revenue and a tax-rate spike to 63.5% left net income down 91% and diluted EPS at $0.03.

Basic EPS fell to $0.03 from $0.98 q/q and $0.56 y/y as net income attributable to Lazard dropped 91% y/y to $4.8M on higher compensation expense and a 63.5% effective tax rate versus 34.1% a year earlier.
Diluted EPS fell to $0.03 from $0.91 q/q and $0.52 y/y for the same reasons as basic EPS — a comp ratio increase to 69.9% and a tax-rate spike to 63.5% from 34.1%.
